support_summary: D5/D6/D1: two researchers both prompted ChatGPT and independently validated citations with disagreements resolved by consensus but no agreement figure reported (Methods); topics author-chosen with list in Multimedia Appendix 1; verification across Google Scholar, PubMed, Google Search and DOI Foundation (Table 2). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D7 settled low; D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1: 120 questions author-developed across 8 radiology subspecialties with no external sampling frame (Methods; Supplementary Material 1); all other domains low - verbatim prompt presented December 2024 with default parameters, Radiologist 1 blinded and did not pose the questions, RAS 0=fabricated defined against Medline/Google Scholar/DOAJ/web searches (Table 2). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled some concerns; Overall settled some concerns. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D5/D6/D3: paper never states who verified the 176 citations or whether verification was duplicated or blinded, and no generation settings are reported (Methods; Table 1); verification source itself was strong and sequential (Google Scholar, then author-list and title searches, plus Scopus/PubMed/WorldCat), but DOI denominator differs between Table 1 (51/135) and Results text (51/141). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled low; D3 settled some concerns. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D2: Bard, Perplexity, SciSpace, Elicit and Bing are named with no version strings and no generation date is stated, so the run cannot be placed in time (Methods); verifier identity and duplicate verification are never reported, and no whole-reference fabricated count is printed - only RHS identifier errors against PubMed/Google Scholar (Tables 2-3). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23: no assessor disagreements on this study; judgements carried over unchanged.]

D1/D2/D3: topics were 50 ChatGPT-suggested proposals screened by five reviewers against FINER criteria, model is named only as ChatGPT (GPT-3) with no generation date, and no generation settings are reported; verification was strong - five researchers independently checked Scopus/PubMed/Google search, discrepancies discussed and resolved, Fleiss kappa 0.959 (Results; Table 3). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled some concerns; D2 settled some concerns; D3 settled no information; D7 settled low; D8 settled low; Overall settled some concerns. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D4/D7: verification was against PubMed alone, so references outside PubMed could be missed, and 'Non-Correct Citations' fold unrelated real references in with unfindable ones without a split (Summary; Table 1); duplicate verification itself was sound - two ophthalmology experts independently validated citations in phase 2 with Cohen kappa 0.74. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D6 settled low; D7 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D5/D6/D3: paper never states who verified the 59 references, whether verification was duplicated or blinded, or any generation settings (Methods; Results); topics were 20 author-chosen medical questions, and only 11 of 18 real references were journal articles, leaving handling of the other real references unclear, though existence was checked on PubMed and journal websites. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D4 settled low; D5 settled no information; D7 settled low; D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1/D8: prompts ran for 19 professors from the university hospital homepage but only the 8 professors ChatGPT recognised contributed the 260 references, and results are printed as percentages only with no counts (Main text; Table 1); prompt is printed verbatim with run dates 16-25 October 2023 and checking was by two observers against PubMed/Web of Science/Google Scholar/Lattes with consensus categorisation. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D2 settled some concerns; D7 settled some concerns. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D5/D6: paper never states who verified references or whether verification was duplicated or blinded - the reported Fleiss kappa measures consistency of chatbot answers across the 3 sessions, not verifier agreement (Table 4; Table 2 testing schedule); topics derived from papers with at least 100 citations lean to established guideline areas, while prompt text and per-arm testing dates are printed. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled some concerns; D2 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D4/D5/D6: no verification source is named anywhere and verifier identity, independence and duplication are all unreported, so fabrication calls (complete vs partial, Methods; Tables 4-5) cannot be checked against a stated source; topics were the full 192-question OrthoBullets SAE set, and video items were excluded because of Copilot limitations. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled low; D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1: two prompt versions were tested for each request and 'the query that led to the largest number of results was retained', i.e. the prompt was selected after seeing outputs (Methods); verifier identity and duplicate verification for the LLM-supplied papers are not reported (the two independent reviewers screened the PubMed systematic-review search only), and 'hallucinated' was defined as any 2 of title, first author or year wrong (Abstract; Table 2). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled some concerns; D2 settled some concerns; D3 settled high; D4 settled some concerns; D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D6: citation validity 'was assessed by a single evaluator' with specialty training and the authors state no inter-rater reliability testing was conducted (Results, citation hallucination assessment; Limitations); verification sources were strong (PubMed, Google Scholar, Web of Science, publisher databases, doi.org) across the full 331-question AAP examination set, but the Results text mislabels the GPT-5.0 IQ arm as 'GPT-4.0 IQ' (Table 5). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D2: DeepSeek is named with no version and no generation date is stated for either model (Table 3; section 3.5); a single conjunctivitis topic was used, verifier identity and duplication are unreported, and further errors (incomplete author lists, wrong issue/volume numbers) are described in text without counts, so partial matches are not counted apart. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled some concerns; D7 settled some concerns; D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D2/D5/D6: no model versions are stated for ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity (data collected 1-30 September 2025 on free-tier web interfaces, Methods) and all RHS scoring was by a single investigator, mitigated by a predefined rubric, a standardised PubMed/Google Scholar workflow and 95% intra-rater agreement on a random 200-reference re-check (Supplementary Material); no fabricated or accurate counts are printed, only RHS means (Tables 2-4). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D5/D6/D8: verification was programmatic against Crossref and PubMed APIs with printed verified/warning/failed/corrupted categories (Table 3), but there was no independent human duplicate check, three arms used unreported system-default models, the authors' own AI Research Army system is one of the arms under test, and several printed hallucination rates do not equal (failed+corrupted)/total from the printed counts (section 3.4). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23: no assessor disagreements on this study; judgements carried over unchanged.]

D2: model is named only as 'ChatGPT (free version)' with no version string and no generation date, and generation settings are never reported (temperature is raised only as a limitation); questions came from the Japanese Physical Therapy Guidelines (5 per section x 3 sections), references were checked by PMID/DOI then title searches on an unnamed database, with two assessors per section and weighted kappa 0.93-0.98 for reference accuracy, though section denominators sum to 38 against a text total of 37 (Table 2). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D2 settled some concerns; D3 settled no information; D4 settled low; D7 settled low; Overall settled some concerns. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1/D4: the 15 topic categories were themselves model-generated rather than drawn from an external frame, and bibliographic score 0 folds non-PubMed-indexed real sources (books/guidelines) in with nonexistent references, although any accessible academic database could also be checked (Methods, Reference assessment; Scoring system); verification was otherwise strong - two independent reviewers, Cohen kappa 0.966, consensus, single session March 2026 with web search enabled. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D2 settled low; D3 settled low; D5 settled some concerns. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1/D7/D4: three ad-hoc topics were probed in interactive conversations in which the model was confronted and re-prompted after its answers were seen, including a request for literature by co-author A. Kleyer (Main text; Figure 1); no verification source is named ('independent literature search' only - PubMed/Scopus/Web of Science appear only inside the quoted AI reply), model version is not stated, and no rule for partially matching references is given, with verifiers being the two authors who ran the chats. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D2 settled some concerns; D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D7/D8: references were classified as verifiable, inaccurate or hallucinated under a stated rule (Methods 3.3) but per-model hallucinated counts are not printed - only per-question hallucination-rate ranges - and inaccurate counts are not given apart per model (Results 4.1); sampling was systematic (first 200 Quora rosacea questions screened by predefined criteria), models are exactly versioned with web search disabled and default configuration, and the evaluating dermatologist was blinded to model identity. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D2 settled low; D6 settled high; D8 settled some concerns; Overall settled high. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D5/D7: references were cross-checked independently by two reviewers on PubMed, Google Scholar and Web of Science with discrepancies resolved by discussion but no agreement statistic, and author contributions show one verifier (DS) also generated the prompts and collected the data (Methods, Reference verification; Table 6); 'False' (n=61) folds fabricated and unverifiable references together with irrelevant real ones, with no split printed. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled some concerns; D6 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D4: fabrication was defined to include 'studies not indexed in PubMed', so verification on PubMed alone builds a coverage gap into the fabricated count itself (Results; Appendix C Table 4); each of the 5 graders also evaluated only citations from responses they themselves generated (single grader per response, element-by-element PubMed match, any discrepancy including minor typographical errors counted equally), though topics were all 70 AAOS CPG recommendations, prompts are in Appendix A, and runs were February-March 2026 on paid ChatGPT-5 with web search available under default settings. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D2 settled low; D7 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D6/D8: all references were independently evaluated by 2 investigators with discrepancies resolved by consensus but, as the authors note, no inter-rater reliability statistic was calculated, and counts are pooled across the 3 prompt types with per-prompt-group results printed only as mean accuracy scores (Table 1 vs Table 3); fabricated was defined as not found in PubMed, Google Scholar or CrossRef, with 0/1/2 accuracy counts printed per model (Tables 3-4). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D3 settled some concerns; D8 settled low. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1: the 10 neurocritical care topics were 'selected by a single domain expert without a formal consensus or Delphi process' and not stratified by evidence density (authors' Limitations); every other domain is low - identical zero-shot prompts on 10 March 2026 via official paid interfaces with retrieval disabled, and two blinded neurocritical care experts independently verified each reference against PubMed, DOI resolver, Google Scholar and CrossRef with Cohen kappa 0.91 and a stated 0-3 Hallucination Scale (Methods; Table 1). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D2 settled some concerns. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D6/D1: reference validation was by a single reviewer with, as the authors state, no inter-rater reliability data, using judgement-based classes (fabricated, misrepresented, accurate/supportive) whose fabricated and misrepresented counts are not printed separately - only the combined 29/88 hallucination count (Table 1; Results, Reference reliability); validation covered a correctness-stratified subsample (all 44 incorrect answers plus 44 randomly selected correct answers) of the 203 OITE questions, with GPT-5 run 29-30 August 2025 at default temperature 1.0 in a new chat per question and checked on PubMed, Google Scholar, Google and librarian-assisted searches. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled low; D6 settled high; D8 settled low; Overall settled high. See robustness/rob-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1: four author-defined cardiology (CRT) topics arranged in a 2x2 maturity/specificity matrix with standardized prompts (Methods), a small hand-picked set in one narrow subdomain; D2: complete prompts in Supplementary Table S2, tools accessed via free web interfaces Aug 2025-Jan 2026, ChatGPT-5 queried using the GPT-5 model; D4/D5/D6: references 'manually verified by the investigators' by DOI and title searches with no verification database named and no duplicate verification of bibliographic accuracy reported - the triple blinded expert rating (Fleiss kappa 0.72) covered relevance, not existence; D7: minor discrepancies classed locatable/corrected and only citations 'not traced to any identifiable source after DOI and title searches' classed hallucinated, counted apart (0 in main analysis; 10/59 in the clinical-studies subanalysis). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D3 settled low; D7 settled some concerns; D8 settled low. See robustness/ft2/rob-new-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1: 10 clinician questions sourced from North American Spine Society guidelines plus 10 author-written patient counterparts (Methods; Supplemental Digital Content 1) - a small guideline-based set; D2: both persona prompts printed verbatim and queries performed October 2025 on default web interfaces, but Microsoft Copilot carries no version (ChatGPT 5.0, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.5, OpenEvidence 2.7.12 are versioned); D3: internet search enabled for all, temperature 'not recorded', and a stated re-prompt rule when more than 5 citations were generated; D5: citations 'manually verified by the authors' with generation/verification roles not separated; D6: three independent medical student reviewers, 95.4% agreement, Cohen kappa 0.918, discordant scores resolved by consensus with the senior author; D4/D7: verification on PubMed and publisher websites across authors/title/year/journal/PMID/DOI, with Score 2 accurate / 1 misrepresented / 0 fabricated counted apart (Table 1). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D8 settled low. See robustness/ft2/rob-new-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D4: 'A fabricated reference was defined as a reference cited by ChatGPT but not indexed in PubMed' (Response Assessment) - fabrication is defined by a single database, so real references outside PubMed are counted fabricated by construction; D1: all 19 recommendations of the AAOS hip fracture CPG were queried (complete enumerated frame) from physician, patient and general perspectives; D2: ChatGPT Version 4o mini free public version, prompts submitted Oct-Nov 2024 in new private browsing windows, but full prompt wording is not printed in the main text; D5/D6: the same 4 medical student graders submitted the prompts and 'independently assessed' responses, with no per-reference duplicate grading or agreement statistic for citation grading; D7: fabrication and field-level inaccuracies (title, authors, journal, year, pages, volume, PMID) defined in Methods and counted apart (Table III). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled low; D3 settled some concerns; D8 settled low. See robustness/ft2/rob-new-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1: 14 author-written questions on a single topic (midshaft clavicle fractures), printed in full in Table 1 (4 patient-focused, 10 clinical); D2: ChatGPT-4o mini prompted on August 31, 2024 with the verbatim Table 1 questions; D3: each question submitted three times the same day in separate chat sessions with all 42 responses and 128 references analysed, but no generation settings are reported; D4: references 'verified through independent searches conducted in MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus' including titles, abstracts, keywords and authors; D5/D6: responses independently evaluated by two registrars (CK, RC) and two senior surgeons (MS, BS) - the author team itself - with no agreement statistic or settlement process reported for reference grading; D7: correct / incorrect (locatable with wrong title, authors, date or journal) / fabricated (could not be located at all) defined in Methods and counted apart (1 / 14 / 113). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D3 settled some concerns; D8 settled low. See robustness/ft2/rob-new-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1: 8 author-written questions on a single topic (Achilles tendon rupture), printed in Table 1 - patient questions 1-4 anticipated from Google Trends searches, clinical questions 5-8 author-written; D2: ChatGPT 3.5 presented with the verbatim questions on February 6, 2024 (Methods; Limitations note the free version used in Australia); D3: each question entered twice with all 16 responses and 47 references analysed, but no generation settings are reported; D4: reference accuracy 'verified by conducting searches across MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus'; D5/D6: responses independently evaluated by two registrars (CK, RC) and two senior surgeons (MS, BS), the author team, with no agreement statistic for reference grading; D7: correct / incorrect (inaccurate title, authors, date or journal) / fabricated (could not be found) counted apart (16 / 19 / 12). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D3 settled some concerns; D8 settled low. See robustness/ft2/rob-new-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D5/D6: the paper never states who verified the 115 citations or whether verification was duplicated or blinded - queries were run by one author (LSM) and citations were 'documented' and title-searched, with no verifier named (Methods); D1: the 47 medications were aggregated from the FDA-approved list and the AAN 2012 guideline, with 5 pre-specified negative controls; D2: prompt printed verbatim ('is [medication] an effective medication for the prevention of migraine? Give 3 citations if they exist'), ChatGPT-3.5, new session with history cleared, queried April 14 and 16, 2023; D3/D4: single run per medication with no generation settings reported, and existence was settled by title searches on Google Scholar and PubMed only, so field-level accuracy beyond the title was not systematically checked; D7: real (33) / hallucinated (76) / real-paper-name with no real citation (6) counted apart. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D3 settled some concerns; D5 settled no information; D6 settled no information; D8 settled low. See robustness/ft2/rob-new-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1: 20 cases author-developed from the most frequent presentations at one restorative dentistry clinic plus textbooks and exam banks, retained only if Lawshe content validity index >=0.62 from 10 experts; D2: exact versions and URLs for all five models (ChatGPT-5, DeepSeek V3.2, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Copilot, Gemini 3 Flash), all accessed December 25, 2025 on free-tier web interfaces, three-step prompt structure with step 2 verbatim but the follow-up reference request only paraphrased; D3: default settings (temperature not manually adjustable), web browsing enabled, history disabled, new session per question, each case queried once with no regeneration; D4: all references searched in PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus and Web of Science, fabricated only if retrievable from no database; D5/D6: reference assessments 'conducted independently by both study authors' (who also prepared and submitted the prompts) with consensus on disagreement but no agreement figure for references - the reported ICC covers the 42 specialists' Likert ratings; D7: four categories (accurate and relevant / partially accurate / misleading-irrelevant / fabricated) defined in Methods and counted apart per model (Table 3). [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D8 settled low. See robustness/ft2/rob-new-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D1: a 40-question bank built from literature and clinical consultation experience, from which 10 high-priority questions were selected by an independent caregiver screening cohort (N=34, cohort A) - priority selection by design, not a random or complete frame; D5: reference authenticity was verified by 2 reviewers (XH and WH), both authors, and who generated the LLM responses is not stated, so generation/verification separation cannot be confirmed; all other domains low - the complete access protocol (URLs, model versions, browser environment, session management, configuration parameters, full Chinese/English prompt set) is in Multimedia Appendix 1, free-tier web interfaces in April 2025, verification followed a PubMed -> CrossRef DOI resolver -> Google Scholar -> CNKI hierarchy by 2 independent reviewers with Cohen kappa 0.702 pre-adjudication and canonical-source reverification, under a 5-category V/PV/F/G/NR scheme counted apart. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D3 settled low; D5 settled some concerns; D8 settled low. See robustness/ft2/rob-new-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D2: the model is named only as GPT-4 (OpenAI) with no version string and no generation period stated, and the interface is not stated - the run cannot be placed in time (Methods); D4: 'Each reference was verified through direct links or a Google search' - 3,250 references checked on a single general web search with no bibliographic database and no second source before 383 were called hallucinated; D5/D6: who applied the Reference Evaluation for AI tool, and whether reference verification was duplicated or blinded, is never stated (the 3 plastic surgeons rated content with NLAT-AI, not references); D1: 354 questions manually collected by the authors from the Hot pages of r/Keloids, r/SCAR and r/PlasticSurgery as of April 6, 2025 plus questions from 3 medical websites; D3: questions input individually in independent sessions with no appended instructions, settings unreported; D7: references are split only into real (2,867) vs hallucinated (383), with no rule or count for real references carrying wrong fields. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D3 settled some concerns; D7 settled high. See robustness/ft2/rob-new-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D3/D5/D6: no generation settings are reported anywhere, and the paper never states who verified the references or whether that verification was duplicated or blinded - the seven ophthalmologists independently rated anonymised reviews for quality/accuracy/bias/relevance (ICC reported), but the authenticity check is described only as 'all cited references underwent a rigorous authenticity check' with no actor (Methods); D1: nine SMILE topics chosen and classified by 3 experts (consensus of at least 2) into researched / controversial / open, three per group, listed in Table 1; D2: the standardised prompt is printed verbatim ('Write a 1,500-word literature review on the topic...'), free/basic versions of GPT-4, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Grok-3 and DeepSeek R1, but no generation date or interface is stated; D4: references 'manually retrieved and verified through academic databases such as PubMed and Google Scholar', the source set left open by 'such as'; D7: True and relevant / True but not relevant / Fictitious counted apart, but no category or rule covers a real publication cited with wrong fields. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D1 settled some concerns; D8 settled low. See robustness/ft2/rob-new-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D7: references 'located within these databases and pertinent to the query content were classified as verified, those unavailable or irrelevant were classified as unverified' (Methods), and Table 5 relabels the unverified count as Fabricated - real but irrelevant references are folded into the fabricated count with no split printed; D2/D5/D6: models are named (Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1-0528, ChatGPT o3-pro, Gemini 2.5 pro, Claude 4.0) and all 110 questions were entered on June 5, 2025 with session resets, but the exam questions are not reproduced and who searched the references, or whether that search was duplicated, is not stated - the two other researchers evaluated answer correctness against the official key; D1: all OMFS multiple-choice questions from the CNMLE dentistry category 2013-2024 (complete frame, n=110); D3: generation parameters fixed for open-source models (temperature 0.7, top_k 40, top_p 0.9), proprietary models at defaults; D4: Chinese references checked in CNKI and Wanfang, English references in PubMed, Web of Science and Google Scholar. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D3 settled some concerns; D4 settled some concerns; D6 settled no information; D8 settled low. See robustness/ft2/rob-new-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D2: 'Terminology was not established in advance, and participants reported chatbot versions inconsistently' - of 5 Claude users 1 reported paid, 2 reported 3.5 and 2 free/unspecified, and Gemini, OpenEvidence and Perplexity users all indicated free or unspecified versions, so each tool arm pools unrecorded versions (Methods); sessions ran Aug-Sept 2024 and both prompts are printed verbatim; D1: only two author-developed prompts (Teach-Back at discharge; neutropenic diet and sepsis) each with three standardised 'additional' follow-ups; D3: prompts repeated three times per tool by 4-7 librarians per tool with OpenEvidence limited to two follow-ups at the free level, settings otherwise unreported; D5/D6: librarians both submitted prompts and verified citations, duplicate checking with a third-researcher tie-breaker is stated only for relevance, not for the hallucination call, and no agreement figure is given; D4: each citation searched in PubMed, the journal if listed, and via web search before being called a hallucination; D7: 'we counted as real any citation for which we found a close/complete match', so field-level partial errors are folded into the real count with no partial count printed. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D4 settled low; D8 settled low. See robustness/ft2/rob-new-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D3: physicians themselves iterated each LLM interactively - 'the number of iterations required by the physician to either achieve LLM generation of a satisfactory response, or discontinue attempting to do so, was documented' - so the verified reports are satisfaction-selected final outputs, iteration counts varied by user and model, 23 LLM reports contained no references despite several prompts, and 4 Gemini reports were lost to a technical malfunction; D1: 27 queries self-selected by purposively sampled physicians from their own complex cases, 20 retained after pre-specified exclusions; D2: GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 and Claude Sonnet 3.5 accessed via standard web interfaces, but no generation dates are stated and the individual clinical queries are not printed; D4-D8 low: existence verified through PubMed and Google Scholar (direct URL for websites) with full-text faithfulness checks, report quality evaluated post-hoc by an independent researcher blinded to report source and to satisfaction, and hallucinated / unfaithful / irrelevant citations counted apart in sequence. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D4 settled low; D7 settled some concerns; D8 settled low. See robustness/ft2/rob-new-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D6: the citation audit is described only as 'an independent post hoc audit of all AI-generated references' - whether it was duplicated or blinded and how disagreements were settled is not stated, and the reported ICCs cover the blinded panel's Likert ratings, not the audit; D5: the audit's performer is not named; D1: two hand-picked topics (chronic rhinosinusitis; infantile subglottic hemangioma, one common and one rare); D2: section-by-section prompt templates in Table 1, standard conversational interfaces with browsing/deep-research features explicitly not enabled, generation in triplicate across April 2025, but models are named only as GPT-4.0 and Gemini 2.0 with no exact release strings; D7: the four audit categories (fully accurate / minor metadata discrepancy / duplicate / fabricated or corrupted) were set in a post hoc audit rather than in advance, though counts are given per model (GPT-4.0 89.6% fully accurate, 0% fabricated; Gemini 2.0 71.7%, 23.9%); D3/D4/D8 low: fresh sessions, identical prompts, the first chronologically generated iteration pre-selected for evaluation, verification against PubMed and journal websites by exact title and author matching, and all topics, styles and models reported. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D2 settled some concerns; D3 settled low; D8 settled low. See robustness/ft2/rob-new-adjudication-log.md for per-domain support lines.]

D4: no verification source or procedure for references is stated anywhere - Gemini's citations are described as '32 PubMed articles... with links provided' and ChatGPT's nonexistent studies were identified narratively, in one case only after a follow-up link request drew an apology, so the fabrication calls rest on no named, systematic check (Methods; Results; Tables III-IV); D1: queries were patient-style rephrasings of the 12 strong- or moderate-strength AAOS glenohumeral arthritis CPG recommendations, with limited-strength and consensus recommendations excluded for a stated reason; D3: each query submitted once on a single day, but all queries went through one continuing anonymous session (authors' limitation: later responses may have been shaped by earlier ones) and links were elicited by follow-up requests; D5/D6: two authors (S.M.O., S.B.P.) independently classified responses with a third tie-breaker and Cohen kappa 0.84, but that duplication covers CPG concordance, not the reference calls, which are unattributed; D7: headline counts fold the two failure modes together ('nonexistent or inappropriately cited': ChatGPT 4/6, Gemini 5/32), separated only in narrative examples; D2 low: models GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Pro, submitted April 30, 2025, queries printed in Table I. [Robustness pass 2026-10-23, RoB adjudication by reading: D3 settled some concerns; D5 settled no information; D8 settled low.
